reasons: Lake identity names the case as Chavez v. Martinez, court U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 2003-05-27, and year 2003.
Lake citations list official cite 538 U.S. 760, parallel cites 123 S. Ct. 1994 and 155 L. Ed. 2d 984, and vendor/neutral cite 2003 U.S. LEXIS 4274.

The opinion states that police questioning does not constitute a criminal case and that compelled statements may not be used at trial, but the Self-Incrimination Clause violation occurs only upon use in a criminal case.

The opinion states Martinez was never made a witness against himself because his statements were never admitted against him in a criminal case, and reverses qualified immunity denial as to the Fifth Amendment claim.
Justice Souter's controlling remand opinion states any damages theory based on outrageous police conduct must sound in substantive due process and that the issue should be addressed on remand.
The opinion centrally discusses unwarned custodial interrogation and states that Chavez gave no Miranda warnings.
The opinion holds that failure to read Miranda warnings to Martinez did not violate his constitutional rights and could not ground a Section 1983 action in this setting.
As a later Supreme Court case applying and limiting Miranda-remedy consequences, the Key-Progeny home role is supported.
The case is a Section 1983 suit and the opinion frames qualified immunity through whether the alleged conduct violated a constitutional right.
The opinion reverses the Ninth Circuit's denial of qualified immunity as to Martinez's Fifth Amendment claim.
The Section 1983 and qualified-immunity home role is directly supported by the opinion text.
The opinion describes Martinez's Fourteenth Amendment substantive due process theory as a claimed right to be free from coercive questioning.
Justice Souter's Court opinion remands whether Martinez may pursue liability for a substantive due process violation.
Related cross-doctrine is appropriately narrower than a key holding label because the due-process claim was remanded rather than finally resolved by the controlling opinion.
Treatment/currency is outside lens A, but the disclosed lake identity verifies court_level scotus and court U.S. Supreme Court.
The authority-weight label Binding — SCOTUS is supported by the disclosed court identity.
